input.rationale: Closed the child question's last stated gap by running the cluster scenario in both restart modes inside one experiment: the same cluster, stores, partition and repair phases, with the restarted node using Config.RestoreCommittedLogs in one run and not in the other. Local construction feedback shows the only difference the mode makes: with the feature on the restarted node reports the stale {A,B,C}, wins the two-voter partition while the other three voters elect their own leader, and applies a write of its own; with the feature off it reports {A,B,C,D,E}, no node leads the two-voter partition, the cluster has a single leader, and the restarted node applies no write at all. The comparisons are therefore declared per mode with separate admissions so the receipt carries the A/B rather than only the defect side.

scope.description: The five-node restart scenario (bootstrap {A,B,C}, committed applies, user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful shutdown of A, partition {A,C} | {B,D,E}, restart of A, healing, repair by snapshot install) executed twice in one run: once restarting A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and once restarting it with the feature off, everything else identical, including that both runs stage the commit index during the first life by running with the feature enabled before the restart.
assumptions: Both runs use freshly created stores and transports; the mode is the only intended difference, and in both runs A's first life runs with the feature enabled so a persisted commit index exists.
The partition, healing and repair phases run identically in both modes; the repair phase triggers a snapshot install in both runs because the leader compacts while the restarted node is cut off.

Recorded rather than asserted: the applied-write metric across nodes is only meaningful when both sides committed a write, so the control comparisons use the restarted node's own applied writes and the leader counts instead of cluster-wide consistency.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The control reproduces the same first-life and partition schedule; it is a control for the restart mode, not for the scenario.
No repository test was executed.

experiment.prefix: The helper builds five InmemTransports in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore and Config with TrailingLogs 0, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and the feature enabled, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A; it starts D and E, adds each as voter, applies one further command and emits 'fixture' (snapshot index and membership, newest configuration entry index and membership, stored commit index, pre-restart configuration and the derived operands). It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores with the mode's restart feature setting and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome' (leaders, terms, leader count, per-node leader booleans, reported configurations, write errors and indexes, payloads, conflicting_commits). It reconnects the mesh, waits for one leader, applies one more entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' (payloads and terms at the conflict index, applied write lists, configurations). It then runs the repair phase: choose a current-configuration leader, cut A off, apply ten commands, snapshot the leader, reconnect A, wait for the snapshot install, wait 300ms and emit 'repaired'. The test runs mode defect_restart first and control_no_restore second, so the event order is fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired, fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired.
semantic_changes: The scenario body moved into a helper that takes the mode and the restart feature flag; the test now runs defect_restart (restart with the feature) and control_no_restore (restart without it) in one execution, emitting the same five events per mode.
Admissions and comparisons are declared per mode so the receipt shows the feature-on and feature-off runs side by side.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: this control isolates the restart's feature setting as the cause of the stale membership and the minority election, since everything else about the two runs is identical.

scope.description: Restart-shaped construction of a single node (LocalID A, ProtocolVersion 3, in-memory log/stable/snapshot stores) whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, observed with RestoreCommittedLogs off, on (construction only), and on with background goroutines started.
assumptions: The stores, configuration contents and their indexes are supplied by the harness: snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1, log entries 1..7 with a LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, and a persisted commit index of 7 (StageCommitIndex), which is a state a follower can reach after committing a configuration change and crashing before taking a newer snapshot.
The FSM discards applied entries and its Restore accepts the snapshot bytes; snapshot restore therefore succeeds and lastApplied after restore is the snapshot index.
For the two construction cases conf.skipStartup is true, so no background goroutine runs and r.configurations is read directly as the state NewRaft computed.

For the live case the node runs normally (default timeouts) with no reachable peers, and the sample is taken only after the node has entered the candidate loop; the public GetConfiguration copy is read instead of r.configurations.
excluded: The election/quorum consequence is not executed here: no election with a majority of the current configuration and a minority of a stale one is run.
The snapshot was produced by the harness rather than by a live Snapshot() call, so the fixture's log/snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: For each mode the harness creates a fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it writes a version-1 snapshot at index 5, term 1 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; it stores log entries 1=LogConfiguration{A,B,C}, 2..5=LogNoop, 6=LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, 7=LogNoop; it calls logs.StageCommitIndex(7). It then emits a 'fixture' event describing those stored facts, builds Config with DefaultConfig(), LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, fsm, logs, stable, snaps, trans). In the two construction modes conf.skipStartup is left true, and a 'construct' event reports lastApplied, commit index, latest/committed configuration id sets and indexes, quorumSize, hasVote(self), the number of batches queued on fsmMutateCh and the number of FSM restores. In the live mode the background goroutines run; a 'live' event reports the public GetConfiguration id set, the node state and current term. Modes run in the order baseline, restore_committed, restore_committed_skip_startup_false so the emitted event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, live.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft startup path: NewRaft's configuration scan (api.go) combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay (api.go restoreFromCommittedLogs -> raft.go processLogs); the node is responsible for using the configuration of the latest configuration entry in its own log.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: the restarted node is responsible for deriving candidate admission and election quorum from the latest configuration entry in its own log, and voters are responsible for granting at most the votes their own view of the configuration requires.

prefix.before: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. prefix.after: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. A repair phase is added after the healed sample: choose a current-configuration leader, cut the restarted node off, commit ten entries, snapshot the leader, reconnect the node, wait up to 15s for it to install a snapshot, then sample the conflict index and applied commands.

A fifth event 'repaired' reports the repair leader, applies, snapshot index, error, whether the snapshot was installed on the restarted node, its applied writes and configuration afterwards, whether the conflict index entry is gone, and the applied writes across the cluster.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster in which node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} so both sides commit at the same index and term, is healed, and is then repaired by forcing a snapshot install from a current-configuration leader while A is temporarily unreachable.
assumptions: All phases are produced through normal operations: bootstrap, election, committed applies, a user snapshot, AddVoter, graceful restart, transport partition and reconnection.
TrailingLogs is 0 for every node, so the leader's snapshot compacts its log beyond the disconnected node's position, which is the condition that makes the leader send a snapshot instead of entries.
The snapshot install is observed through the restarted node's own last-snapshot index and its applied commands; the leader and the other nodes are not modified by the harness during the repair phase.
The repair phase records rather than asserts which current-configuration node leads: leadership is transferred to B only if the healed leader is not a current-configuration node.

The harness is a revision of the one used for the split-brain and applied-state experiments (adding the repair phase and TrailingLogs 0); the earlier comparisons remain recorded with those experiments' own receipts.
excluded: No user Restore, no compaction without a lagging follower and no term-changing truncation is exercised; only the snapshot-install path is.
The scenario stops after the first repaired sample; C is not repaired in the same run.
No on-disk store or crash is exercised and no repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore and Config with TrailingLogs 0, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. It starts D and E, adds each as voter, applies one further command and emits 'fixture'. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome'. It reconnects the full mesh, waits for one leader, applies one further entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' with payloads, terms, applied write lists and configurations. It then runs the repair phase: it selects a leader among B, D and E (transferring leadership to B if the healed leader is not one of them), cuts A from every other node, applies ten commands on that leader, takes a snapshot on it, reconnects A, waits up to 15s for A's last snapshot index to reach the leader's snapshot index, waits 300ms and emits 'repaired'. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft recovery path: the leader's snapshot plus log compaction (removeOldLogs/compactLogs with TrailingLogs 0) and the follower's installSnapshot handling, which restores the FSM and replaces the log and configuration.

comparisons.description: The ordinary recovery path should engage once the stale node falls behind a compacted leader: the node installs a snapshot.
After the snapshot install the restarted node's applied state should match the current configuration's side.
The command only the minority side had accepted should no longer be in the restarted node's applied state.
The divergent entry at the conflict index should be gone from the restarted node's log after the install.
The installed snapshot also carries the committed configuration, so the stale view should be gone afterwards.
Negative half of the answer: a node that stayed up to date is not repaired by another node's snapshot install, so the cluster's applied state should still differ.

semantic_changes: The scenario body moved into a helper that takes the mode and the restart feature flag; the test now runs defect_restart (restart with the feature) and control_no_restore (restart without it) in one execution, emitting the same five events per mode.
Admissions and comparisons are declared per mode so the receipt shows the feature-on and feature-off runs side by side.

scope.description: The five-node restart scenario (bootstrap {A,B,C}, committed applies, user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful shutdown of A, partition {A,C} | {B,D,E}, restart of A, healing, repair by snapshot install) executed twice in one run: once restarting A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and once restarting it with the feature off, everything else identical, including that both runs stage the commit index during the first life by running with the feature enabled before the restart.
assumptions: Both runs use freshly created stores and transports; the mode is the only intended difference, and in both runs A's first life runs with the feature enabled so a persisted commit index exists.
The partition, healing and repair phases run identically in both modes; the repair phase triggers a snapshot install in both runs because the leader compacts while the restarted node is cut off.

Recorded rather than asserted: the applied-write metric across nodes is only meaningful when both sides committed a write, so the control comparisons use the restarted node's own applied writes and the leader counts instead of cluster-wide consistency.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The control reproduces the same first-life and partition schedule; it is a control for the restart mode, not for the scenario.
No repository test was executed.

basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: this control isolates the restart's feature setting as the cause of the stale membership and the minority election, since everything else about the two runs is identical.

comparisons.description: Feature on: the restarted node should use the committed configuration entry in its own log.
Feature off control: the same restart without the replay should use the committed configuration.
Feature on: the two-voter partition should not be able to elect a leader.
Feature off control: the same partition should not elect a leader.
Feature off control: the cluster should have exactly one leader.
Feature on: the restarted node should not have applied a write of its own that the current configuration never accepted.
Feature off control: the restarted node should have applied nothing of its own.

semantic_changes: The healed event now also reports each node's applied command list (MockFSM applied data filtered to the two conflicting write payloads), whether those lists agree, and the restarted and majority nodes' applied writes.
Three comparisons are added over the healed event: the applied writes must agree across nodes, and the two operand comparisons confirming which write each side applied.

The scenario body moved into a helper that takes the mode and the restart feature flag; the test now runs defect_restart (restart with the feature) and control_no_restore (restart without it) in one execution, emitting the same five events per mode.
Admissions and comparisons are declared per mode so the receipt shows the feature-on and feature-off runs side by side.
